source.title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems

accepted.question_text: For a closed manifold M of dimension at least 2, can the real-analytic diffeomorphisms Diff^ω(M) be classified up to topological conjugacy by complete invariants, and is the topological-conjugacy equivalence relation on Diff^ω(M) Borel?

evidence.quote: Question 1.1 (Gorodetski). Is there a way to provide a classification of real analytic diffeomorphisms Diffω(M) of a given closed manifold M, dim M ≥ 2, by complete invariants? Is the equivalence relation on Diffω(M) given by topological conjugacy Borel?

accepted.question_text: Can the space of Kupka-Smale diffeomorphisms of a given closed manifold be classified up to topological conjugacy by complete invariants, and is topological conjugacy a Borel equivalence relation on that space?

evidence.quote: Question 1.2 (Gorodetski). Can the space of Kupka-Smale diffeomorphisms of a given closed manifold be classified up to topological conjugacy by complete invariants? Is topological conjugacy a Borel equivalence relation in the space of Kupka-Smale diffeomorphisms?

accepted.question_text: For a manifold M with dim M ≥ 2, does there exist an open dense subset or a dense Gδ subset of Diff∞(M) on which the equivalence relation of topological conjugacy is Borel?

evidence.quote: Question 1.3 (Gorodetski). Is there an open dense subset (or a dense Gδ subset) in Diff∞(M), dim M ≥ 2, such that the equivalence relation given by topological conjugacy on the subset is Borel?

accepted.question_text: What is the descriptive-set-theoretic complexity of the topological-conjugacy relation for Axiom A dynamical systems?

evidence.quote: Question 1.4 (Foreman). What is the complexity of the relation of topological conjugacy of Axiom A systems?

accepted.question_text: Let C be the collection of diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold M that are topologically conjugate to a structurally stable diffeomorphism, and let E be topological conjugacy restricted to C. Is E Borel reducible to equality?

evidence.quote: Question 1.5 (Foreman). Let C be the collection of diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold M that are topologically conjugate to a structurally stable diffeomorphism. Let E be the relation of topological conjugacy restricted to C. Is E Borel reducible to ≈ (equality relation)?

accepted.question_text: Is the topological-conjugacy relation on the class of all Cantor minimal systems a Borel equivalence relation?

evidence.quote: Question 1.6 (Gao). Is the topological conjugacy relation for all Cantor minimal systems Borel?

accepted.question_text: Is the topological flip-conjugacy relation on the class of all Cantor minimal systems a Borel equivalence relation?
accepted.context_brief: Flip conjugacy on Cantor minimal systems

evidence.quote: Question 1.7 (Gao). Is the topological flip conjugacy relation for all Cantor minimal systems Borel?

accepted.question_text: For all minimal subshifts, is topological conjugacy hyperfinite, or is it instead a universal countable Borel equivalence relation?

evidence.quote: Question 1.8 (Gao). Is the topological conjugacy relation for all minimal subshifts hyperfinite or a universal countable Borel equivalence relation?

accepted.question_text: Is there an algorithm that decides whether two subshifts of finite type are topologically conjugate by homeomorphisms?

evidence.quote: Question 1.9 (Foreman). Is there an algorithm for determining whether two subshifts of finite type are conjugate by homeomorphisms?

accepted.question_text: Does an analogue of the stated almost-Borel classification remain true when one discards only sets of zero Lebesgue measure and uses metric entropy instead of topological entropy, at least in dimension 2?
accepted.context_brief: Almost Borel classification with metric entropy

evidence.quote: Question 1.15 (Buzzi). I conjecture that a similar statement also holds when discarding only sets of zero Lebesgue measure using metric entropy instead of topological entropy (see [36]), at least in dimension 2 where we have the recent result [6].

accepted.question_text: When measure isomorphism is restricted to K-automorphisms, is it a Borel equivalence relation, and can it be reduced to an S∞-action?

evidence.quote: Question 1.16 (Newberger). Is measure isomorphism restricted to K-automorphisms a Borel equivalence relation? Can it be reduced to an S∞-action?

accepted.question_text: Is the measure-isomorphism relation on ergodic measure-preserving transformations of the unit interval bi-reducible with the maximal Polish group action?

evidence.quote: Question 1.17. Is the measure isomorphism relation on ergodic measure-preserving transformations of the unit interval bi-reducible with the maximal Polish group action?

accepted.question_text: Where does Kakutani equivalence on ergodic measure-preserving transformations lie among analytic equivalence relations, and is it reducible to an S∞-action?

evidence.quote: Question 1.18. Where does the Kakutani equivalence relation on ergodic measure-preserving transformations sit among the analytic equivalence relations? Is it reducible to an S∞-action?

accepted.question_text: For integers k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1, what is the descriptive complexity of the set CPE^k(T^n) of C^k self-maps of the n-torus with completely positive entropy?

evidence.quote: Question 2.2 (García-Ramos). Let k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1. What is the complexity of CPEk(Πn)?
We say f ∈ Ck(X, X) has completely positive entropy if every non-trivial factor has positive topological entropy. We denote the set of such functions with CPEk(X).

accepted.question_text: For integers k ≥ 0 and n ≥ 2, is the class CPE^k(T^n) ∩ Mix of mixing C^k self-maps of the n-torus with completely positive entropy a Borel set?
accepted.context_brief: Mixing maps with completely positive entropy

evidence.quote: Question 2.5 (García-Ramos). Let k ≥ 0 and n ≥ 2. Is CPEk(Πn) ∩ Mix Borel?
We say f ∈ Ck(X, X) has completely positive entropy if every non-trivial factor has positive topological entropy. We denote the set of such functions with CPEk(X).

accepted.question_text: For every smooth mixing map f ∈ C∞(T^2, T^2), is the measure of maximal entropy fully supported?
accepted.context_brief: Measures of maximal entropy on T^2

evidence.quote: Question 2.6 (García-Ramos). Is the measure of maximal entropy fully supported for every smooth mixing map on the torus (f ∈ C∞(Π2, Π2))?

accepted.question_text: Are Kakutani equivalence classes Borel sets, and if they are, what is the complexity of the isomorphism relation restricted to a Kakutani equivalence class?

evidence.quote: Question 2.7 (Rodriguez Hertz). Are Kakutani equivalence classes Borel? If so what is the complexity of the isomorphism relation on that class?

accepted.question_text: Let X be the space of continuous actions of the free group F2 on two generators. Is the collection of actions that are measure isomorphic to Bernoulli F2-actions a Borel set?

evidence.quote: Question 3.1 (Foreman). Let X be the space of continuous actions of the free group F2 on two generators. Is the collection of Bernoulli actions measure isomorphic to Bernoulli F2-actions a Borel set? (Borel actions?)

accepted.question_text: Let X2 be the free part of the full shift {0,1}^{Z^2} with shift action σ, let XH be the space of directed bi-infinite Hamiltonian paths in Z^2, and let Φ : (X2, σ) → (XH, σ) be a Borel equivariant map as in Theorem 3.2, inducing a Z-action T_Φ on X2. Can Φ be chosen so that for all invariant ergodic probability measures μ and ν on X2, the systems (X2, μ, σ) and (X2, ν, σ) are conjugate if and only if (X2, μ, T_Φ) and (X2, ν, T_Φ) are conjugate?

evidence.quote: Theorem 3.2. [20] There is a Borel equivariant map Φ from (X2, σ) to (XH, σ). One of the consequences of this result is that it gives a (very special) orbit equivalence from (X2, σ) to a Z Polish dynamical system which we denote henceforth by (X2, TΦ). In addition one has that if µ is an invariant ergodic probability measure for (X2, σ) then it is also an invariant ergodic probability measure for (X2, TΦ). Let Me denote the space of invariant probability measures for (X2, σ).
Question 3.3 (Chandgotia). Can Φ be chosen such that for all µ, ν ∈ Me, (X2, µ, σ) is conjugate to (X2, ν, σ) if and only if (X2, µ, TΦ) is conjugate to (X2, ν, TΦ)?

accepted.question_text: Is the conjugation action of Aut(X, μ) on itself a complete orbit equivalence relation, meaning that every orbit equivalence relation induced by a Borel action of a Polish group on a standard Borel space is Borel reducible to it?

evidence.quote: In general, given a Borel action of a Polish group on a standard Borel space we consider the induced orbit equivalence relation. We say that an orbit equivalence relation E is complete if every orbit equivalence relation is Borel reducible to E.
Conjecture 4.1 (Sabok). The action of Aut(X, µ) on itself by conjugation is a complete orbit equivalence relation.

accepted.question_text: Fix an ergodic measure-preserving transformation T0 on a standard probability space (X, μ), and let [T0] be its full group, consisting of bimeasurable bijections U : X → X that send each point to another point in its T0-orbit. If T1 and T2 are Bernoulli shifts with equal entropy and the same orbits as T0, does there exist T ∈ [T0] such that T1 = T T2 T^{-1}?

evidence.quote: Let us first fix an ergodic transformation T0, and define its full group [T0] as the group of bimeasurable bijections U : X → X such that for all x, the point U(x) belongs to the T0-orbit of x.
Question 4.2 (Thouvenot). Let T1, T2 be two Bernoulli shifts with equal entropy, suppose that they have the same orbits as T0. Is there T ∈ [T0] such that T1 = T T2T−1?

accepted.question_text: For a fixed ergodic transformation T0 with full group [T0], does the conjugacy relation on Aut(X, μ) Borel reduce to the conjugacy relation on [T0]? Does this remain true after restricting both sides to ergodic transformations?
accepted.context_brief: Reducing conjugacy to a full group

evidence.quote: Let us first fix an ergodic transformation T0, and define its full group [T0] as the group of bimeasurable bijections U : X → X such that for all x, the point U(x) belongs to the T0-orbit of x.
Question 4.3. Does the conjugacy relation on Aut(X, µ) Borel reduce to the conjugacy relation on [T0]? Does it when we restrict to ergodic transformations?

accepted.question_text: Is the conjugation action of Aut(X, μ) on itself unbalanced in the sense of Allison and Panagiotopoulos, and if so does this remain true after restricting to ergodic transformations?

evidence.quote: Actually, their work also provides a dynamical analogue of turbulence called unbalancedness which rules out Borel reduction to equivalence relations coming from actions of Polish groups admitting a compatible biinvariant metric, so a positive answer to the following question implies a negative answer to Question 4.3.
Question 4.4. Is the conjugacy action of Aut(X, µ) on itself unbalanced? If yes, is it still if we restrict to ergodic transformations?

accepted.question_text: For a fixed ergodic transformation T0 with full group [T0], is the conjugacy relation on [T0] Borel? If not, does it become Borel after restricting to ergodic transformations?
accepted.context_brief: Borel complexity inside a full group

evidence.quote: Let us first fix an ergodic transformation T0, and define its full group [T0] as the group of bimeasurable bijections U : X → X such that for all x, the point U(x) belongs to the T0-orbit of x.
Question 4.5. Is the conjugacy relation on [T0] Borel? If no, is it when restricted to ergodic transformations?

accepted.question_text: For the topological full groups arising from continuous actions of Polish groups on compact Polish spaces, especially actions of the real line, what general structure results hold? In particular, when are these groups coarsely bounded, when do they admit a dense finitely generated subgroup, how many such groups are there, and can one classify their actions by homeomorphisms?
accepted.context_brief: Topological full groups of Polish-group actions

evidence.quote: More generally, one can use the approach from [8] to show that given a Polish group G acting continuously on a compact Polish space X, one can associate to it a Polish group, the topological full group of the action.

Question 4.6. What can we say about these topological full groups, especially when the acting group is the real line? For instance, when are they coarsely bounded in the sense of [37]? When do they admit a dense finitely generated group? How many such groups are there? Can one classify their actions by homeomorphisms?

accepted.question_text: Let Auth^{<∞}(I, λ) be the space of Lebesgue measure-preserving automorphisms of the interval with finite entropy, and let Diff(T^n, λ^n) be the space of Lebesgue measure-preserving diffeomorphisms of the n-torus. Is there a Borel map G from Auth^{<∞}(I, λ) into the disjoint union over n of Diff(T^n, λ^n) such that each system (I, λ, T) is measure-isomorphic to (T^n, λ^n, G(T))?

evidence.quote: Let (I, λ) be the interval Lebesgue space and (Πn, λn) the n-torus Lebesgue space. We have that Auth<∞(I, λ) is the space of (Lebesgue) measure-preserving automorphisms of I with finite entropy and Diff(Πn, λn) the space of (Lebesgue) measure-preserving diffeomorphisms of Πn.
Question 5.1 (Rodriguez Hertz). Is there a Borel map G : Auth<∞(I, λ) → ⋃n Diff(Πn, λn), such that (I, λ, T ) is isomorphic to (Πn, λn, G(T )).

accepted.question_text: With the same notation as in Question 5.1, is there a Borel map G from Auth^{<∞}(I, λ) into the disjoint union over n of Diff(T^n, λ^n) such that each system (I, λ, T) is Kakutani equivalent to (T^n, λ^n, G(T))?

evidence.quote: Let (I, λ) be the interval Lebesgue space and (Πn, λn) the n-torus Lebesgue space. We have that Auth<∞(I, λ) is the space of (Lebesgue) measure-preserving automorphisms of I with finite entropy and Diff(Πn, λn) the space of (Lebesgue) measure-preserving diffeomorphisms of Πn.
Question 5.2 (Rodriguez Hertz). Is there a Borel map G : Auth<∞(I, λ) → ⋃n Diff(Πn, λn), such that (I, λ, T ) is Kakutani equivalent to (Πn, λn, G(T )).

accepted.question_text: If a measure-preserving dynamical system is Kakutani realizable by a smooth toral system, must it also be realizable up to measure isomorphism?

evidence.quote: Question 5.3 (Rodriguez Hertz). If a measure-preserving system is Kakutani realizable can we conclude it is also isomorphically realizable?

accepted.question_text: Does every measure-preserving action of a free group admit a uniquely ergodic topological model?
accepted.context_brief: Uniquely ergodic models for free-group actions

evidence.quote: Question 5.4 (Seward). Do we have uniquely ergodic topological models for every measure-preserving group action of a free group?

accepted.question_text: Which families of dynamical systems are universal in the sense discussed in the paper?

evidence.quote: Question 5.5 (Rodriguez Hertz). Which families of systems are universal?

accepted.question_text: Let (T^d, R) be a toral automorphism that is ergodic for Lebesgue measure, and let (Y, S) be a homeomorphism of a Polish space with no invariant probability measure. Does there exist an equivariant Borel embedding of (Y, S) into (T^d, R)?
accepted.context_brief: Borel embeddings into ergodic toral automorphisms

evidence.quote: Question 5.6. [10] Let (Td, R) be a toral automorphism which is ergodic for the Lebesgue measure. Let (Y, S) be a homeomorphism of a Polish space without any invariant probability measure. Is there an equivariant Borel embedding of (Y, S) into (Td, R)?

accepted.question_text: Let (T^d, R) be a toral automorphism that is ergodic for Lebesgue measure, and let (Y, S) be a homeomorphism of a Polish space with no invariant probability measure. Does there exist an equivariant Borel map from (Y, S) into the free part of (T^d, R)?
accepted.context_brief: Maps into the free part of ergodic toral automorphisms

evidence.quote: Question 5.7. [10] Let (Td, R) be a toral automorphism which is ergodic for the Lebesgue measure. Let (Y, S) be a homeomorphism of a Polish space without any invariant probability measure. Is there an equivariant Borel map of (Y, S) into the free part of (Td, R)?
